# SB-1007 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2, line P2-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L4-HP03

Hazard description
Blasting operations in the Heat Treat area generate airborne particulate that can penetrate local exhaust and general ventilation systems during upset conditions or when containment is compromised. Fine dust increases risk of respiratory exposure, contaminant carry into downstream machining, and accelerated wear of hydraulic system seals through ingress to adjacent spaces. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P2-L4-HP03) is 320 bar. Loss of filtration or uncontrolled dust migration can lead to unplanned maintenance and increased safety incidents.

Affected equipment
Primary: EQ-P2-L4-HP03 (Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #3) located on line P2-L4.  
Secondary: adjacent conveyors, local extraction hoods, and portable breathing air housings in the P2 Heat Treat zone. Refer to SOP-P2-L4-01, SOP-P2-L4-02, and SOP-P2-L4-03 for routine operation and cleaning sequences that interface with blasting and press activities.

Required controls
- Containment: Maintain intact blasting curtains and negative-pressure hooding during blasting. Inspect curtain integrity before each shift; remove visible breaches and tag until repaired per SOP-P2-L4-01.  
- Ventilation: Confirm local exhaust is operating and filters are installed per manufacturer recommendations. Replace prefilters when loading is observed; do not bypass filters. See SOP-P2-L4-02 for ventilation verification steps.  
- Housekeeping: Implement immediate vacuuming with HEPA-rated units after blasting; do not use compressed air for cleaning near EQ-P2-L4-HP03. Follow cleaning checklists in SOP-P2-L4-03.  
- Isolation: When blasting occurs, isolate hydraulic access panels on EQ-P2-L4-HP03 and verify seals are engaged. Prevent dust ingress to hydraulic components and respect the system pressure limit of 320 bar during any pressure-related work.  
- PPE: Mandatory respiratory protection and eye protection for personnel within the Blast Exclusion Zone; ensure fit testing and training records are current per site requirements.  
- Monitoring: Increase airborne particulate monitoring during blasting campaigns and log results in maintenance records. Escalate excursions for corrective action.

Effective date
Rev B (effective on issuance of this bulletin)
